semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: The term 'transformer architectures' is often interchangeably used with 'transformer models', which represent the structure and design of transformer-based methods.

parent_domains.justification: Transformers are a type of neural network architecture, focusing on attention mechanisms for sequence-to-sequence tasks.
Deep learning architectures encompass various neural network designs, including transformers, CNNs, and RNNs.

closest_parent_domain.justification: The term 'neural network architectures' is most directly associated with 'transformer architectures' as they specifically belong to the broader category of network structures within neural networks, without the broader coverage of all deep learning types.

child_domains.justification: A 'transformer language model' is a specific application of transformer architectures, focusing on language tasks.
Graph transformer is an application of the transformer architecture applied to graph-structured data.
These models specifically utilize transformer architectures in graph-based learning tasks.
They represent specific implementations of transformer architectures, tailored for processing graph data.

closest_child_domain.justification: Transformer language models are one of the most common and prominent applications of transformer architectures, best exemplified by models like BERT and GPT.

sibling_domains.justification: Neural architecture search relates to methodologies for finding optimal neural network architectures, which include transformers.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Among the sibling domains, 'neural architecture search' is closely related because it encompasses methods that can optimize or design transformer architectures.

unrelated_domains.justification: Power systems do not relate to transformer architectures within neural networks.
Hardware design is unrelated to the software architecture of transformers.
Scattering transforms are a different conceptual approach unrelated to transformer architectures.
This domain pertains to a different field and is not related to neural network architectures.
Although transformers can be applied to signal tasks, signal processing as a domain broadly covers many techniques outside the scope of transformers alone.
Image processing is a different application domain, not specifically a part of transformer architectures.
FPGA synthesis pertains to hardware, unrelated to the architectural study of transformers.
While transformers can be used in image synthesis, the domain itself is broader and distinct.
